name: ならまちテラス食堂 蜜や (Naramachi Terrace Shokudo Mitsuya)

claims.text: Fried foods (karaage), hamburger, curry and noodle dishes are core menu items, so wheat is widespread in the kitchen and shared fryer/prep contamination is likely. No gluten-free handling is documented.
As a Japanese set-meal diner, standard wheat-containing soy sauce is used in seasoning and sauces (e.g. the sweet-vinegar sauce on the fried chicken); no wheat-free soy sauce is indicated.

The menu centers on meat (pork, chicken, Yamato beef) and homemade roasted pork, and sets use fish/meat dashi and miso, so plant-based meals are not separated and contact with animal products is unavoidable.

name: 奈良町豆腐庵 こんどう (Naramachi Tofu-an Kondo)

claims.text: Set meals are documented to include fu (wheat gluten) and dengaku with miso, so wheat is present in the kitchen and in standard courses.
Oboro tofu and other dishes are served with dashi soy sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce is documented, so standard soy sauce (typically containing wheat) should be assumed.
Courses include items such as ganmodoki/hirousu and clear soup; the dashi base is not documented as plant-based, so fish/bonito dashi should be assumed unless confirmed.
Tofu is made from 100% domestic soybeans and sea nigari with no documented additives, and many courses are plant-based tofu, yuba and vegetable preparations.

name: 奈良めし 板焚屋 三条店 (Narameshi Itadakiya (Sanjo))

claims.text: No gluten-free handling or fryer information is published; the menu is built around soy-sauce-based grilling, tempura, and simmered dishes, so wheat cross-contact should be assumed throughout.
Yakitori/grilled and simmered izakaya dishes typically use standard wheat-based soy sauce and tare; no gluten-free seasoning is indicated.
Dishes are prepared in a meat-and-fish kitchen and most use dashi or soy seasoning, so vegetable items are not reliably vegan; no separation is documented.
An English menu is available, making it easier for a non-Japanese-speaking diner to identify and ask about ingredients.
Menu is dominated by breaded deep-fried items (fried shrimp, tonkatsu, beef cutlet) sharing fryer oil, plus flour-based demi-glace and curry, so wheat cross-contact is pervasive.
Kitchen centers on meat and fish-dashi-based dishes; no separation for plant-based diets is documented.
Wheat noodles are the core product and are boiled in shared water; broth and tare contain fish and likely wheat-based soy sauce. No gluten-free accommodation indicated.
Niboshi/chicken ramen and tsukemen are seasoned in the standard Japanese ramen style, which uses wheat-containing soy sauce-based tare.
All broths are made from dried fish and chicken; toppings include pork chashu and egg. No vegan items.
The kitchen is built around vegetables and seasonal produce, and a vegetarian menu is available, so plant-leaning diners have real choices.
Ancient red rice and brown rice are used as the standard staple, which are naturally gluten-free bases.

name: 二代目 出雲そば だんだん (Nidaime Izumo Soba Dandan)

claims.text: Soba shop serving buckwheat noodles and tempura; no documented gluten-free handling. Wheat-based tempura and soy-based tsuyu are part of the menu.
Traditional soba is served with tsuyu/dipping sauce, which is typically soy-sauce based (contains wheat) and fish dashi.
Menu features fish and sashimi alongside soba; dashi-based broths are used throughout.
An all-wheat bakery where every product contains flour and loaves use whole-grain wheat; flour is airborne throughout, making it unsafe for celiac or gluten-sensitive diners.

The bread range mixes plant-based hard breads with butter/egg/dairy items (croissants, melon pan, kouglof, cheese breads), all produced in one small kitchen, so cross-contact between vegan and non-vegan items is likely.
Bread is made with house-cultured natural yeast and domestic, organically grown pesticide-free wheat milled into whole-grain flour — a transparent, additive-conscious approach to ingredients.
